Its ID, name, status, text and seeAlso fields agree with the claimed correspondence. The decoded citation is https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/automake.git/tree/lib/texinfo.tex?h=v1.16.5#n23

The GitHub Git object API for SPDX’s data repository reports tag v3.29.0 and object.type commit with the exact claimed target. The captured response has SHA-256 9695bf0c0fae8f1db7f1bee44d2176c06a045a3fb62f1ab9aa4b4cef283ebd13. GitHub reports the tag as unsigned. Repository provenance supports the tag-to-commit observation without establishing a verified signer.

The complete commit-pinned Automake specimen matches the claim’s file digest. Lines 23–26 provide the source side of the comparison, including “when this file is read by TeX,” “a Texinfo source document,” “the result without restriction,” and the section 7 sentence. The file’s preceding GPL grant falls outside the text transcribed by SPDX.

challenge.method: I tested two possible edition errors by distinguishing the annotated SPDX tag object from its target commit and reading the decoded GNU source citation for its project, path, release, and line anchor. I then compared the actual exception text with the header. SCES §7 requires an exact external revision and recognition of derivative sources.
challenge.results: Tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. That commit appears in the generated JSON locator. The decoded citation selects v1.16.5#n23, where the inspected specimen begins the matching paragraph. No substantive wording discrepancy emerged.

limitations: The result is documentary correspondence in SPDX 3.29.0. Byte equality and formal SPDX template matching were outside the claim.
SPDX is the authority for its identifier and release status. Its quotation shares the GNU notice’s lineage and supplies no independent corroboration of the grant.
